answer: Admission of a kth identity in one grove requires an echo against every earlier identity, and each echo burns one walnut. Ten identities burn forty-six walnut: forty-five echo, one per pair, plus one founding echo; a first identity burns one. No grove may record the same echo twice, and a second grove must record an echo for each identity on the old list, so splitting or restarting adds the same pairs instead of avoiding them.
